text:
maria_support: FYI customer ABC reports broken streaming when traffic passes through their gRPC gateway + Envoy. Works fine if they hit Redwood directly (curl --http1.1), but in-prod they see repeated disconnects and truncated SSE events. They're seeing partial JSON payloads and client-side 'unexpected EOF'.

ben_runtime: ack — can you paste the minimal repro and headers from the customer? any proxies between client and our edge?

maria_support: Copied customer notes: 'Browser client connects -> goes through company's grpc-gateway (translates to http/1.1 to our API) -> Envoy -> Redwood. When the client connects via curl -N --http1.1 directly to Redwood it's stable. When routed through their infra we get intermittent disconnects and only first 1-2 events before stream terminates. Reconnects create duplicate partial events.' They also attached a HAR and this curl:

curl -v -H 'Accept: text/event-stream' -H 'Authorization: Bearer REDACTED' --http2 https://internal-gateway.example.com/v1/stream

and when they force http1.1:

curl -v -H 'Accept: text/event-stream' -H 'Authorization: Bearer REDACTED' --http1.1 https://internal-gateway.example.com/v1/stream

first works (via http1.1), second via http2 gets truncated.

carla_success: hmm browsers will prefer http/2.0 so they can't rely on forcing http1 in prod. customer is asking if Redwood supports SSE over http2 fully.

ben_runtime: short answer: SSE semantics are defined for http1 chunked transfer-encoding; h2 uses DATA frames so it can work, but intermediaries often break expectations (buffering, conversion, grpc-gateway translating streaming RPCs). common culprits: grpc-gateway buffering responses, envoy's http2/1.1 codec misconfig, nginx proxy_buffering on, or a gateway turning streaming into unary responses with content-length.

maria_support: customer logs: 'Read loop error: unexpected EOF' and this server log snippet from their gateway:

```
[grpc-gateway] translating response -> buffering up to 8KB before flush
[envoy] upstream reset, reason: connection termination
```

so it looks like buffering + a reset.

dan_sre: ask them to check these quick things:
- confirm that the gateway is not aggregating the whole response (content-length present?). if so, it's not streaming.
- nginx: ensure `proxy_buffering off; proxy_http_version 1.1; chunked_transfer_encoding on;` for the route.
- envoy: check `use_downstream_protocol: true` and `http2_protocol_options` vs http1 bridge config. also make sure `stream_idle_timeout` isn't too low.

ben_runtime: also watch for grpc-gateway specifics — if they're using grpc -> http1 JSON gateway, it often buffers because it maps gRPC streaming to multiple HTTP responses unless configured for bidi streaming. If their gateway uses HTTP/2 to talk upstream and then translates, it might be closing streams early.

maria_support: I sent the customer this repro checklist and asked for: tcpdump of TLS session (or server-side proxy logs), their gateway config, and a short curl test that forces both http1 and http2 directly to our edge and to their gateway.

ben_runtime: some concrete troubleshooting steps we should recommend in-thread:
1) On customer's gateway/proxy: disable response buffering. If nginx:
```
location /v1/stream {
  proxy_pass https://redwood-upstream;
  proxy_buffering off;
  proxy_cache off;
  proxy_http_version 1.1;
  chunked_transfer_encoding on;
  proxy_set_header Connection ""; # avoid adding upgrade/connection headers
}
```
2) If using Envoy as edge: ensure route is configured with `use_downstream_protocol=true` (so h2->h2 preserves streaming semantics) or make the gateway speak plain http1.1 to Envoy to preserve chunking semantics.
3) Check for any gRPC->HTTP gateway that is converting streaming RPCs to buffered HTTP responses. Prefer native gRPC streaming or a websocket alternative for browser clients.

carla_success: can we provide a short server-side tweak on our side to help detect broken intermediaries? maybe return a small 'probe' SSE comment periodically or include an example header the client can echo back?

ben_runtime: we can add diagnostic headers on our streaming endpoint to detect buffering: e.g., send `x-rw-sse-probe: 1` early and then flush. But note: some proxies will strip unknown headers. Another option: emit a small comment line `:probe\n\n` every 10s to assert liveness — but that doesn't fix drop mid-request.

maria_support: customer asked about reconnect behavior — they want resume semantics. we don't have tokenized resumption for SSE; best practice is idempotent events with `id:` fields so client can dedupe on reconnect. suggested to add `id` on each event and for clients to include Last-Event-ID on reconnect.

dan_sre: assign to eng-runtime to add better logging when a stream is reset by an upstream, and to record whether the reset happened while data was in-flight. ben, can you take a look? tag me when you have a plan.

ben_runtime: taking it. immediate plan:
- add a debug flag to streaming handler that logs upstream->downstream resets with connection-level reason and bytes sent/received.
- add optional periodic comment probe emission for customers who opt-in via query param `?stream_probe=1` (helps detect buffering/terminations).
- docs: guidance for proxies (nginx/envoy/grpc-gateway) and sample configs.

maria_support: perfect. I told the customer we're implementing a `stream_probe` flag and sent nginx/Envoy snippets. customer will test and get back with gateway config + logs.

deploy-bot: deploy queued: runtime/streaming-debug-flag -> staging (PR #4221)

ben_runtime: i'll post when staging results in the thread. cc @dan_sre @carla_success

maria_support: thanks team — i'll update the case and keep monitoring. :thumbsup:
